messages:
incident-bot: autopage fired -> prom_scrape_errors prod cluster. alert: prometheus_scrape_job_failure_count > 50 for 5m. PD: PD12345
Maya: seeing the autopage. paging oncall now. any obvious blips from deploys? :eyes:
Liam: no deploys in the last hour, I just checked CI. grafana shows scrape_success dropping around 03:12 UTC.
Ash: logs from scrape-proxy show a bunch of 502/503s to s3-buckets for the scrape export blob store. attaching tail: `2026-03-15T03:12:08Z ERROR upload failed: 503 SlowDown`
Riley: curious — is this the kinesis -> s3 pipeline or the prometheus remote_write? could be either.
Maya: PD notif says 'prometheus scrape job failures', so likely exporter -> prometheus scrape targets timing out. check exporter logs and scrape-proxy.
Liam: running `kubectl -n observability logs deploy/scrape-proxy -f --since=5m` now. lots of repeated `PutObject 503 SlowDown` from s3.uploader.
Ash: that indicates S3 503 throttling. we saw increased retries earlier today in metrics. suspect an upstream rate/IO spike.
Riley: customers might see missing alerting and dashboards. need to assess impact. any dashboards with missing critical metrics?
Maya: alerting for some internal dashboards degraded. no customer-facing product alerts observed yet but some customers ingest metrics via our hosted scrape endpoints — they may have gaps.
incident-bot: PD update: page PD12345 acknowledged by Liam at 03:16 UTC. escalation paused.
Liam: acked. I've added ops_lead and infra to the PD. stepping through runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/metrics-s3-throttle
Ash: short term mitigation: switch exporter shards to local disk buffering and reduce concurrent upload threads. can patch scrape-proxy config to lower parallelism. I can push a cold config change to reduce upload concurrency to 2. ok?
Maya: do it. post rollout command and monitor. also enable read-only fallback for dashboards from cached TSDB if available.
Liam: applying config change: `kubectl patch deploy/scrape-proxy -n observability --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"scrape-proxy","env":[{"name":"MAX_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY","value":"2"}]}]}}}}'`
Riley: thanks — also toggling remote_write backpressure to 0.5 to slow down writes from prometheus to the uploader.
Ash: config applied, scrape-proxy pods rolling. logs now show fewer concurrent uploads and reduced 503 rate. `2026-03-15T03:19:25Z WARN retrying upload (retry=1)` but success rate improving.
Maya: monitoring dashboards — scrape_success recovery trend improving at 03:21. still intermittent.
incident-bot: PD update: PD12345 note added by Ash: reduced concurrency to 2; monitoring.
Liam: kicking off a consumer scale for the ingestion workers as a precaution — `k scale deploy ingest-consumers --replicas=8 -n logging`. should help clear backlog.
Ash: consumer scale started. kafka consumer lag shows backlog decreasing from ~120k to ~60k after scale.
Riley: starting customer impact sweep: querying last 1h of hosted-scrape metrics. so far ~2% of customers report metric gaps (non-critical dashboards). emailing affected customers template.
Maya: good. set PD priority to P2 for now; we'll rotate to monitoring once backlog <10k and scrape_success > 99% for 10m.
ops_lead: thanks team. please add a post-incident note with root cause hypothesis (S3 throttling due to spike) and mitigation steps we took. also follow-up with infra to request S3 account throttle increase / retry budget.
Liam: adding notes to PD and the incident channel. I'll prepare a short customer-facing blurb for support.
Maya: status update in 10. if things hold, we can resolve and close PD in ~30m. :thumbsup:
Riley: quick reminder: runbook suggests enabling regional failover for scraper uploads if S3 errors persist. adding to action items.
incident-bot: PD12345 resolved by Liam at 03:43 UTC. final note: reduced upload concurrency + scaled consumers cleared backlog; observed improved scrape_success; recommended infra follow-up.
Maya: closing thread here. postmortem to be scheduled tomorrow with infra and eng-runtime. thanks all for fast response. :heart:
